title: ICAB C2 - Assurance
summary: Explains the concept, purpose and legal framework of assurance, internal controls, obtaining evidence, and professional ethics and acceptance under ISA.

all.name: Full Syllabus Tracker
all.blurb: Official 2025 Syllabus chapter and topic tracker for Assurance. Track your study progress across all syllabus areas.

stages.title: Area 1: Concept, Process & Need for Assurance
stages.name: Area 1: Concept, Process & Need for Assurance
stages.description: Five elements of assurance, levels of assurance (reasonable vs limited), and statutory audit requirements.

nodes.name: Assurance Framework & Audit Demand
nodes.description: Definition of assurance engagement, the 5 elements (three parties, subject matter, criteria, evidence, written report), reasonable vs limited assurance, audit expectations gap, and benefits of assurance.
topics: Definition and objectives of assurance under IAASB Framework
The 5 elements of an assurance engagement
Reasonable assurance (audit) vs Limited assurance (review)
Inherent limitations of audit: Sampling, human error, collusive fraud, estimates
The expectations gap: Audit role vs public misconception
Statutory audit requirements under Bangladesh Companies Act 1994
learningOutcomes: Identify the 5 elements of an assurance engagement.
Distinguish between reasonable and limited assurance conclusions.
Recognise the inherent limitations of assurance.
checklists: Master 5 elements diagram and criteria definition
Review statutory audit appointment rules under Companies Act
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 2: Internal Controls & Information Flows
stages.name: Area 2: Internal Controls & Information Flows
stages.description: Internal control components (COSO), transaction cycles, IT controls, and deficiencies.

nodes.name: Internal Control Framework & IT Controls
nodes.description: Five components of internal control (Control environment, Risk assessment, Control activities, Information & communication, Monitoring); General IT controls vs Application controls; Revenue, Purchases, and Payroll transaction cycles.
topics: COSO Internal Control components and auditor evaluation
Control activities: Authorization, Segregation of duties, Physical, Reconciliations
General IT controls (access security, backups, change management)
Application IT controls (input checks, batch totals, sequence checks)
Sales and revenue cycle controls and testing
Purchases and payments cycle controls and segregation
Payroll system controls and employee verification
Identifying internal control deficiencies and management letter recommendations
learningOutcomes: Explain the 5 components of internal control.
Differentiate general IT controls from application controls.
Evaluate internal controls across sales, purchases, and payroll cycles.
checklists: Analyze sales and purchases cycle control flowcharts
Practice identifying control weaknesses in 5 case scenarios
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 3: Gathering Evidence on Engagements
stages.name: Area 3: Gathering Evidence on Engagements
stages.description: Financial statement assertions, audit procedures (AEIOU), substantive testing, and documentation.

nodes.name: Audit Procedures, Assertions & Testing
nodes.description: Sufficient appropriate audit evidence (relevance and reliability); management assertions for classes of transactions and account balances; audit procedures: Analytical, Enquiry, Inspection, Observation, Recalculation/Reperformance (AEIOU); test of controls vs substantive testing; sampling fundamentals; audit working papers.
topics: Sufficient appropriate evidence: Quality vs quantity, reliability hierarchy
Management assertions: Occurrence, Completeness, Accuracy, Cut-off, Classification, Existence, Rights & Obligations, Valuation & Allocation
Audit procedures (AEIOU): Inspection, Observation, External confirmation, Recalculation, Reperformance, Analytical procedures, Inquiry
Substantive testing for Tangible Assets, Inventory, Receivables, Payables, Cash
Bank confirmation letters and direct receivables circularisation
Inventory count attendance procedures (ISA 501)
Audit documentation: Working papers, retention, and confidentiality
learningOutcomes: Map audit procedures to specific financial statement assertions.
Evaluate the reliability of internal vs external evidence.
Design substantive audit tests for assets, liabilities, income, and expenses.
checklists: Memorize all 8 audit assertions for P&L and Balance Sheet
Draft substantive audit program for inventory valuation and receivables
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 4: Professional Ethics & Acceptance
stages.name: Area 4: Professional Ethics & Acceptance
stages.description: IESBA Code of Ethics, ethical threats and safeguards, client acceptance, engagement letters, and reporting.

nodes.name: Professional Ethics, Threats & Acceptance
nodes.description: Ethical threats (Self-interest, Self-review, Advocacy, Familiarity, Intimidation); safeguards; independence requirements; client acceptance and continuance checks; money laundering procedures; engagement letters (ISA 210); unmodified vs modified audit reports.
topics: Fundamental principles: Integrity, Objectivity, Competence, Confidentiality, Behaviour
The 5 ethical threats and concrete safeguards in assurance
Auditor independence of mind and appearance
Client onboarding checks: Integrity, competence, legal capacity, AML/KYC
Communication with predecessor auditor (professional clearance)
Engagement letters: Purpose, contents, and agreement of terms (ISA 210)
Overview of auditor reporting: Unmodified report structure vs modifications
learningOutcomes: Identify ethical threats and formulate appropriate safeguards.
Evaluate acceptance of new assurance engagements.
Explain the purpose and key contents of an engagement letter.
checklists: Practice 15 scenario questions on ethical threats and safeguards
Review standard engagement letter clauses under ISA 210
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)
